defect: An address was treated as an account. One iPhone authenticated on 192.168.77.139, was switched off for days and returned on 192.168.77.102; the .139 Session stayed ACTIVE and netd went on renewing its nft authorization. DHCP had meanwhile reissued .139 to a different device (d6:5a:1c:d2:12:d6, hostname 'ipad', lease to 2026-08-29T13:11:06Z), so for that window a device that never authenticated held an address the appliance was authorizing, and any traffic it sent would have been forwarded and metered onto the absent guest's entitlement. Whether it transmitted is not provable from the single accounting sample; the exposure is structural.
rules_implemented: The Entitlement is the authority for service limits, whatever authentication method produced the subject. IP and MAC are connection evidence and neither is the account nor the quota owner.
A device may receive different addresses over time, and doing so resets nothing: no new Purchase, no new Entitlement, no usage back to zero. Proven against a real database.
All Sessions under one Entitlement spend one aggregate data/time quota, while per-Session accounting detail survives for attribution.

Device limits apply across the Entitlement. A private or randomised MAC is simply a device the property has not seen, handled by the existing device-authorization policy rather than treated as a person.

An address is never renewed once it is no longer demonstrably the device's: the producer retires an attachment when its device appears at a newer address (SUPERSEDED_ON_DEVICE_MOVE), and the applier verifies ownership against DHCP before every renewal, withdrawing authorization and closing the Session through the controlled writer when it is foreign (ADDRESS_NO_LONGER_OWNED).
A Session's IP and accounting identity are never rewritten mid-series: a moved device gets a NEW Session under the same Entitlement rather than an edited old one.
Evidence outage is not evidence: when DHCP cannot be asked, nothing is torn down and the gap is reported.
speed_allocation: Migration 0059 adds service_plan_revisions.speed_allocation, immutable with the revision it belongs to. PER_DEVICE is the default and preserves exactly what every existing revision was sold as. SHARED gives the Entitlement ONE aggregate ceiling: an HTB parent class per entitlement with each session a child holding a small guaranteed floor and the group's ceiling, so an active device borrows the whole ceiling when the others are idle. Deliberately not a division into fixed per-device portions.
